subject: Renewal: Oxford Health — EU onramp + APAC sovereign fallback questions
messages:
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@oxfordhealth.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@oxfordhealth.com
Date: 2027-08-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal window — EU onramp + APAC fallback behavior

Hi Kimberly,

Our renewal is coming up in September and we'd like to include two items in the amendment:

1) Add an EU primary deployment (for customer-facing traffic originating in EU).
2) Add APAC as a warm failover for traffic spikes / region outages, but with strict residency constraints — during any APAC failover, EU-origin data must not be stored at rest in APAC.

We currently run with you on the hosted plan (see attached current_usage_report.csv). Can you confirm:
- Rough timeline to stand up EU primary and APAC warm-failover?
- Pricing delta for reserved capacity + a short-term surge window?
- Practical approaches to ensure EU data residency during failover (key separation, proxying, tokenization)?

We need this in writing for procurement. If you can attach a draft SOW + estimated pricing, that would be great.

Thanks,
Sarah Lee
Head of Platform Operations
Oxford Health

From: ben.carter@redwood.com

Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-02T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal window — EU onramp + APAC fallback behavior

Quick capacity/pricing notes from infra:

- Baseline: Oxford's current average qps and token volumes in the report support a single EU pod at 2x baseline (reserved) to meet latency SLOs. Recommend reserved pool sized at 2x current steady-state, with a 2-week burst bucket for events.
- APAC warm standby: lightweight warm nodes (KV-only priming) + ability to scale to full replicas within 20-30m. Cost model: +25% monthly on top of EU reserved for warm-standby insurance; surcharge for actual failover traffic (token rate pricing).

Residency approach options (pros/cons):
1) Key-separated mirror (recommended): EU data encrypted with EU-only KMS; in APAC we can route calls through a proxy back to EU for any write/persist operations. Read-only state in APAC is possible with tokenization.
2) In-memory failover only: keep KV cache ephemeral in APAC; any persistence (logs, usage metrics with customer PII) are proxied or dropped. This is lower cost but increases cross-region latency during heavy failovers.
3) Full-data mirror with geo-sanitization: replicate pseudonymized records to APAC; more complex and requires legal sign-off.

I'll attach a draft SOW and an estimate matrix — see draft_sow_redwood_eu_apac.pdf and pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx. Marcus: confirm whether our offer can include a contractual commitment to "no at-rest EU PII in APAC" (control + monitoring/alerting).

-ben
Ben Carter
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: marcus.lin@redwood.com
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-03T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal window — EU onramp + APAC fallback behavior

Confirming controls and proposed contractual language.

- Technical control: We can commit to a mechanism where any data written under the "EU-resident" tag is encrypted with an EU KMS key (customer or Redwood-managed). APAC nodes will accept traffic but will not be able to unwrap the EU KMS keys — they only hold transient, encrypted KV entries. Persistence to object store from APAC is disabled for EU-tagged objects.
- Auditability: We'll enable an audit log stream showing any failover events and a daily digest of keys used/attempted decrypts. We can surface that to Oxford via the Console.
- Contractual language proposal: "During an APAC failover, Redwood will not persist at-rest personal data originating from EU jurisdictions in APAC regions. Any required persistence will be routed to the customer's EU KMS or proxied to EU storage. Redwood will provide audit logs of failover events on request."

Risks / tradeoffs:
- Cross-region latency for writes during failover if proxied (estimated +150–300ms per write).
- Testing required: 2-week failover test window to validate telemetry and prove no-at-rest behavior.

I'll sign off on adding the clause to the SOW. Neha — please add the pricing options (reserved + surge) and finalize the amendment language. Laura — propose pilot dates (I'd suggest Sept 6–20).

-marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Engineer, Infra & Security
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@oxfordhealth.com>, procurement@oxfordhealth.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-04T15:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal window — EU onramp + APAC fallback behavior

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear ask. Below is a concise proposal and next steps.

Summary proposal:
- EU primary: provisioned EU pod, reserved capacity sized at 2x current steady-state.
- APAC warm-failover: warm standby nodes + autoscale to full replicas on failover; persistent storage for EU-tagged data will be disabled in APAC.
- Residency guarantee: contractual clause: "Redwood will not persist at-rest personal data originating from EU jurisdictions in APAC regions during failover; persistence will be routed to the customer's EU KMS or proxied to EU storage."
- Pilot test window: 2 weeks (recommended Sept 6–20) to validate failover behavior and audit logs.
- Timing: EU primary ready in ~6 weeks after SOW sign; APAC warm-standby in ~10 weeks.
- Estimated delta: +25% monthly for APAC warm insurance, reserved pricing uplift for EU pod (see attached pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx for options: 2x, 3x reserved). One-time onboarding & SOW fee in draft_sow_redwood_eu_apac.pdf.

Next steps:
1) I attach a draft SOW and the pricing matrix for procurement.
2) If that looks good, we can issue an amendment and DocuSign link for signature (see related DocuSign link).
3) Schedule the 2-week pilot in the Sept window; we'll coordinate runbooks and a dry-run week prior.

Questions you raised:
- Can EU data be kept out of APAC at rest? Yes — implementation: EU-tagged data is encrypted with EU-only KMS keys; APAC nodes will only hold transient encrypted caches and will proxy writes back to EU storage if persistence required. We'll include audit logs and a daily digest for compliance.

Attachments: draft_sow_redwood_eu_apac.pdf, pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx

Happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk procurement through the SOW if helpful.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
